art_instructions: Inside the cozy Greek classroom at child eye level, frame a wide view that includes the open exit door on the right and familiar classroom elements on the left. On the right third, a wooden door with a soft blue painted frame swings outward to a bright courtyard; a warm sun patch spills across the stone floor and a low step is visible outside. Owl (chibi, 2–3 heads tall), mottled brown-and-cream with a small green scarf and a tiny satchel worn crossbody, is mid-step over the threshold: front talon extended, wings slightly raised for balance, head turned toward the outside with a small, happy smile and bright amber eyes. Place Owl one body-length from the right edge, overlapping the doorway so it’s clear she is exiting; add a couple of soft motion lines behind her tail feathers. The left half shows honey-colored low desks grouped on a colorful woven rug; chairs are neatly tucked in, and on the nearest desk sits her simple crayon picture of a tree and sun from earlier plus a cup of chunky crayons (no letters anywhere). In the back left, hint at a small teacher’s podium with a blue-and-white pottery piece, and set a green potted plant beneath a large sunlit window. Keep walls a soft pastel blue with warm yellow trim accents; use minimal cel-shading with gentle occlusion under feet and furniture. Maintain the Korean aegyo cute style—smooth monoline, rounded shapes, large glossy eyes—and keep the background simple but fully filled with the wall, rug, furniture, and light so the “leaving” action reads instantly.
